vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.6.5

The agent-chronicle skill is a well-structured tool designed to help AI agents maintain a reflective diary. It functions by gathering context from local session logs (memory/*.md) and using OpenClaw's native sessions_spawn mechanism to generate journal entries, which are then stored and managed locally. The included scripts (generate.py, setup.py, and export.py) perform standard file operations and use external tools like pandoc (with the --sandbox flag) for document conversion, all of which are strictly aligned with the stated purpose. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious code execution, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are internally consistent with a diary/journal purpose; it reads agent memory, prepares generation tasks for a platform-native sub-agent, and exports local markdown to PDF/HTML — there are no obvious attempts to exfiltrate secrets or contact unexpected remote endpoints, but a few maintenance and privacy-relevant details deserve attention.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary) aligns with required binaries (python3) and the included scripts. The scripts focus on collecting session logs, persistent diary artifacts (quotes, curiosity, decisions), building generation payloads for an OpenClaw sub-agent, saving markdown entries, and exporting to PDF/HTML — all expected for a journaling skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to read session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md), diary persistent files (memory/diary/*.md), and to spawn a sub-agent via sessions_spawn to perform generation. Reading and writing the agent's memory directory is expected for a diary skill, but this is broad access to any data stored under memory/. The scripts also suggest using pandoc/weasyprint and include an option that references an external CSS URL for HTML export (https://cdn.simplecss.org/simple.min.css), which can be fetched during export. No instructions ask for unrelated secrets or system-wide reads.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec (instruction-only in the registry), so no remote binaries are downloaded by the skill itself. The repository contains Python scripts that run locally. External dependencies (pandoc, texlive-xetex, weasyprint, python-markdown) are required for exporting; installation is left to the operator. No suspicious download URLs or archive extraction are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, which matches the registry metadata. However, multiple scripts attempt to read OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE env vars to locate the workspace/memory directory; these env vars are used (fallbacks to common paths) but not listed as required in metadata. Access to the memory/ directory is intrinsic to the skill's function, but users should be aware that diary generation may ingest any content present in memory/, which can include sensitive data. No other unrelated credentials or secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill flags in registry are default (always:false, user-invocable:true) so it is not force-enabled globally. The skill writes config.json under its skill directory during setup and creates diary files under the chosen diary_path (under workspace/memory/diary/ by default) — expected persistence for this feature. It does not modify other skills' configs or request elevated system privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: read your agent session logs and diary artifacts, build a generation task for a platform sub-agent, save entries to memory/diary, and export to PDF/HTML. Before installing: 1) Confirm you are comfortable with the skill reading/writing the agent’s memory/ directory (it will ingest memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md and persistent diary files). 2) Review config.json privacy settings (memory_integration, privacy_level) to avoid accidentally publishing sensitive summaries to other agent memory. 3) Note the scripts check OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE / AGENT_WORKSPACE environment variables (not declared in metadata) to find the workspace — ensure those point to the intended workspace. 4) If you use export features, be aware exporting may require installing pandoc/weasyprint and may fetch an external CSS URL; run the export tools in an environment you trust. 5) Minor maintenance smells: version strings differ across files (skill.json, package.json, SKILL.md/README), which suggests sloppy release hygiene — not a security issue but worth noting. If you need higher assurance, inspect the scripts in your environment and run them in a sandboxed workspace first.
llm.findings: [pre-scan-injection-none] expected: Static pre-scan detected no injection signals. The code files are present and their behaviors (reading/writing memory, preparing tasks for sessions_spawn) are consistent with a journaling skill.
